phase.description: REVISED (iteration 1; boundary rules added iteration 2): anchor on WHERE THE DEFECT LIVES - the spec/build/verify/ops artifact or process that is defective - NOT where the failure surfaced, was noticed, or was caught. Exactly one value per record. The iteration-2 boundary rules (R1-R3, below) take precedence over the v1.1 generic instrument reading wherever they apply.

spec.belongs: The defective artifact is a governing/design/protocol DOCUMENT or plan: briefs, specs, preregistrations, authorizations and their estimates, protocols, design assumptions, documentation whose stated content diverges from reality (wrong pointers, stale figures, arithmetic slips, two documents disagreeing).
spec.does_not_belong: Constructed code/config content that was merely built badly (build); checking instruments and their recorded outputs (verify); execution-layer failures (ops).
spec.tie_break: Ask 'which artifact is wrong?'. If the answer is a document's CONTENT (it says X, reality is Y), spec - even if a build/verify activity surfaced it. If the document is right and code diverges from it, not spec.

build.belongs: The defective artifact is CONSTRUCTED content: scripts, generators, builders, rules encoded in code, code written against unvalidated assumptions, and - per iteration-2 rule R3 - binding quota/cap ENFORCEMENT LOGIC that mis-enforces (the enforcement code is the defective artifact; the breach it allowed is evidence).
build.does_not_belong: Defects in checking/recording instruments as instruments or in their recorded outputs/data products (verify); document-content defects (spec); runtime/execution-layer failures and blocking capability absences (ops).
build.tie_break: R3 worked example (iteration 2): a per-judge day cap enforced per-class instead of cumulatively, letting the smoke breach 11 vs 10 -> build (the enforcement logic is the defective artifact; the breach is evidence). Contrast: a cap/check whose logic is correct but whose recorded output is wrong stays verify. A mis-budgeted run/config resource (e.g. frozen max_tokens vs thinking burn) is also build - the config is the defective artifact.

verify.belongs: The defective artifact is a checking/measuring/RECORDING instrument, its recorded outputs, or its MEASURED DATA PRODUCTS: validators, classifiers, metrics, rubrics, gates, liveness checks, header scans, value-recording registries/summaries/envelopes/determinism proofs, and measured data products recorded by such instruments (wrong denominators, ERR transcribed as 0, stale recorded hashes, degenerate thresholds, vacuous 0/0 results poisoning a recorded data product) - even though such instruments are themselves coded during build activities.
verify.does_not_belong: The defect under inspection (that lives in build/spec/ops); quota/cap enforcement logic that mis-enforces (build, R3); runtime/execution-layer failures and blocking capability absences (ops).
verify.tie_break: Worked examples: a value-recording registry built wrong (ERR rows transcribed as hits:0) -> verify; a header-scan instrument recording wrong dtype claims -> verify; a degenerate gate printing 0/0 on empty input -> verify; NaN from degenerate 0/0 written into a recorded data product -> verify (recorded output, iteration 2); a determinism proof embedding stale recorded hashes -> verify (v1.1 literal; the iteration-1 build label for this case was a classifier application error, corrected in iteration-2 labels). If the record's subject is 'the check/record/data product said X and X was wrong/absent', verify.

ops.belongs: The defective layer is EXECUTION/run-time or the environment an activity depends on: serving, downloading, scheduling, machine contention, resource exhaustion at runtime of EXTERNAL tools, external-tool runtime crashes, path/OS traps during execution, credential handling during operations, collection services corrupting data at run time, and - per iteration-2 rule R1 - a capability/tool ABSENCE that BLOCKS an activity (the defect lives in the environment; no defective agent artifact exists), and - per rule R2 - an obtained external artifact that is not what it claims to be.
ops.does_not_belong: Runtime exhaustion caused by one's own code/config budgeting (build, per the tie-break below); document defects (spec); instrument/data-product defects (verify).
ops.tie_break: Worked examples: an external pinned converter crashing at load with ValueError -> ops; machine contention from other tenants -> ops; MSYS /tmp not resolving for native Python at execution -> ops. R1 worked example (iteration 2): MSI packaging blocked because WiX is not installed on the machine -> ops (blocking capability absence; no defective agent artifact). R2 worked example (iteration 2): an external 'abliterated' checkpoint failing its anchor gate because it does not match its claimed base twin -> ops (the artifact in use is not what it claims). Contrast (R2): a check session degraded by external conditions while its controls remain intact is verify - the checking process is the subject and it worked. Runtime exhaustion of a resource one's OWN code/config mis-budgeted keeps the earlier phase (build for configs/code, spec for protocol math).

iteration_2_boundary_rules.rule: A capability/tool ABSENCE that BLOCKS an activity is ops: the defect lives in the environment and no defective agent artifact exists.
iteration_2_boundary_rules.worked_example: MSI packaging remains a known gap because WiX is not present on the machine -> ops (blocks the packaging activity; nothing the agent built is defective). Contrast: a present tool crashing at runtime is also ops (v1.1 example); a tool the agent built that misbehaves is build/verify per the instrument/data-product rules.

iteration_2_boundary_rules.rule: Anchor on the record's SUBJECT: a check/search/measurement session degraded by external conditions while its controls remain intact -> verify (the checking process is the subject and it worked); an obtained external artifact that is not what it claims -> ops (the defective thing is the artifact in use, not the checking layer that caught it).
iteration_2_boundary_rules.worked_example: A rarity battery degraded by engine throttling/403s with positive controls barring false zeros -> verify; an external checkpoint failing its anchor gate because it differs from its claimed base twin -> ops.

iteration_2_boundary_rules.rule: A binding quota/cap mis-enforced by CODE is build: the enforcement logic is the defective artifact; the breach it allowed is evidence, not the defect.
iteration_2_boundary_rules.worked_example: A per-judge day cap enforced per-class instead of cumulatively (smoke breached 11 vs 10) -> build. Contrast: a cap/check whose logic is correct but whose recorded output is wrong stays verify.

cause_class.description: Single dominant root-cause class. Exactly one value; residual candidates flagged in notes as kappa calibration data. REVISED (iteration 1): verification_gap is NOT a catch-all - run the tie-break order below and only land on verification_gap if no earlier rule fires and the defect is checking-shaped.
tie_break_order: 1. Finite resource consumed but unaccounted (VRAM, RAM, disk, compute time, TOKENS, budget bytes/percent)? -> resource_blindness

2. A definite value/verdict recorded or carried where truth was unknown or different (ERR transcribed as hits:0; estimator artifacts read as physics; unverified estimates entering authorizations)? -> precision_overclaim
3. Document/spec/protocol content diverging from reality (stale figures, wrong pointers, documented rule != actual behavior, two documents disagreeing, arithmetic slips in briefs)? -> spec_drift
4. A success claim resting on the agent's own broken or uncontrolled verification? -> self_confirmation
5. Failure to obtain or bind the right external thing (gated/401/403/404, deleted repos, dead URLs, wrong reference file compared, token scope)? -> retrieval_failure

6. Execution environment differing from assumptions (contention, missing tools, third-party tool bugs, upstream limitations, external artifacts not matching their documentation, throttling)? -> environment_drift
7. A secret/credential exposed to observation without confirmed compromise? -> credential_exposure
8. Else, if the defect is checking-shaped (a check missing, unwired, unexercised, or too coarse)? -> verification_gap
9. Nothing fits? -> other:<slug>, marked PROPOSED in notes; the kappa audit promotes or kills it

verification_gap.belongs: A CHECK was missing, unwired, opt-in instead of enforced, added but never exercised, or too coarse: unwired code paths, unexercised parameters, untested end-to-end wiring, degenerate/unvalidated instrument behavior, missing guards or assertions, metadata-contract compliance not checked before submission.
verification_gap.does_not_belong: Wrong definite values recorded (precision_overclaim); document content contradicting reality (spec_drift); unaccounted resource/token burn (resource_blindness); success claims on own broken evidence (self_confirmation).
verification_gap.tie_break: Must be checking-shaped: name the check that was missing/misfiring. Worked examples: an opt-in ctx guard -> verification_gap; output-path param added but never exercised -> verification_gap; degradation policy recorded but apply_degradation never called -> verification_gap. NON-examples (iteration 1): ERR (403) transcribed as hits:0 -> precision_overclaim; README count stale + wrong spec pointer -> spec_drift; thinking-mode token burn vs frozen max_tokens -> resource_blindness.

resource_blindness.belongs: A finite resource was consumed but not accounted when planning or configuring: VRAM/RAM/disk budgets, compute-time-infeasible protocol bases, class-wide floors exceeding byte budgets, and TOKEN burn (e.g. a thinking template exhausting a frozen max_tokens budget).
resource_blindness.does_not_belong: External contention nobody budgeted (environment_drift); missing tools (environment_drift).
resource_blindness.tie_break: Worked example (iteration 1): model burns all 256 tokens thinking, empty content (F-027/F-081-type) -> resource_blindness, NOT verification_gap: the budget simply did not account the burn.

spec_drift.belongs: Document/spec/protocol content diverges from reality or from what was built: wrong design assumptions, stale figures propagating into artifacts, documented rules that the code does not actually follow, wrong cross-references/pointers in specs, two documents disagreeing, dimensionally-wrong formulas, brief arithmetic slips.
spec_drift.does_not_belong: Coding errors against a correct spec (verification_gap, if checking-shaped); wrong recorded INSTRUMENT values that are not document claims (precision_overclaim).
spec_drift.tie_break: Worked examples (iteration 1): documented record_id rule verifies 0/94 records because code nulls the id first (documented rule != behavior) -> spec_drift; stale README test count + wrong selfpref items_file pointer -> spec_drift; two documents disagreeing on the accepted-set size -> spec_drift. A document right when written that later went stale through missed maintenance is verification_gap (the maintenance check was missing), not spec_drift.

self_confirmation.belongs: The agent recorded or relied on evidence of success generated from its own uncontrolled or incorrect verification (false replay claims, mechanism demos that demo nothing, batteries without controls).
self_confirmation.does_not_belong: A broken instrument overclaiming regardless of claim direction (precision_overclaim); a simply-missing check (verification_gap).
self_confirmation.tie_break: Was there a success-claim resting on the agent's own evidence? Yes -> self_confirmation.

retrieval_failure.belongs: Failure to obtain or bind the right external thing: gated/401/403/404 resources, deleted repos, dead URLs, wrong reference files compared against, token scope, wrong task-to-artifact mapping, folklore citations.
retrieval_failure.does_not_belong: Missing local tooling or capabilities (environment_drift); failing to check something already held (verification_gap).
retrieval_failure.tie_break: Artifact exists but fetched/compared/paired wrongly, or cannot be obtained at all -> retrieval_failure; environment lacks a capability -> environment_drift.

environment_drift.belongs: The execution environment differs from what the plan/code assumed: machine contention, OS/shell traps, missing tools (Docker, WiX), third-party tool bugs, upstream software limitations, external artifacts or repos not matching their documentation, platform instability, throttling/rate limits.
environment_drift.does_not_belong: Resource shortfalls from one's own budgeting (resource_blindness); access denials to specific artifacts (retrieval_failure).
environment_drift.tie_break: External world not matching assumptions -> environment_drift.

precision_overclaim.belongs: A number, verdict, or transcription carried more certainty than warranted: estimator artifacts read as physics, definite values recorded where truth was unknown or different (ERR transcribed as hits:0), unverified estimates entering authorizations/records, wrong definite figures asserted in prose (element-count typos, wrong hunk counts).
precision_overclaim.does_not_belong: Wrong values from buggy logic with no certainty claim (verification_gap); success-claims from self-referential evidence (self_confirmation).
precision_overclaim.tie_break: Worked example (iteration 1): DDG rows recording ERR (403) as hits: 0 -> precision_overclaim, per the explicit boundary rule; a review asserting 'exactly 3 hunks' when there are 4 -> precision_overclaim.

credential_exposure.status: FULL CLASS (promoted from PROPOSED other:credential-exposure at audit iteration 1; dual-classifier iteration-0 agreement 1.0 on its single member)
credential_exposure.belongs: A secret/credential/token was exposed to observation (on-screen, in logs, in shared artifacts) WITHOUT a confirmed compromise event; the associated duty is rotation/hygiene. The record must disclose the exposure incident and the rotation/hygiene disposition, never the secret itself.
credential_exposure.does_not_belong: Actual credential compromise or misuse (out of dataset scope); failed authenticated fetches (retrieval_failure); secrets handled per protocol with no exposure (not a failure).
credential_exposure.tie_break: retrieval_failure requires a failed fetch; environment_drift requires a wrong environment assumption; neither covers hygiene incidents - that gap is exactly what this class covers.

other:<slug>.status: PROPOSED - created only when a documented failure fits NO class after the tie-break order; must be marked PROPOSED in the record notes; the kappa audit promotes or kills each proposal.
other:<slug>.belongs: Only documented failures with no defensible home in the eight classes above.
other:<slug>.does_not_belong: Anything resolvable via the tie-break order with a flagged ambiguity - prefer flagging.
other:<slug>.tie_break: Write the decision rule the new class would need; the audit compares it against existing classes.

detection_layer.description: Which layer first CAUGHT the failure (not which layer committed it). Exactly one value.

self_caught.belongs: The agent that owned the failed work caught it - including via its own smoke tests, gates, positive controls, dry-runs, reconciliation, honest self-disclosure - before or after shipping. CLARIFIED (iteration 1): this includes a data steward/reviewer-role agent catching defects in its OWN tooling (the owner of the tool caught it); the owning agent of the failed artifact is whoever produced the thing that failed.
self_caught.does_not_belong: Failures first surfaced by a genuinely separate second context over the owner's artifact.
self_caught.tie_break: Worked example (iteration 1): a steward's validator flags 3 FAILs that are all validator defects, caught when the steward reruns/inspects its own validator -> self_caught (the steward owns the validator; no second context reviewed the steward). Worked example (counter-case): a worker's item builder defect caught by the adversarial reviewer's scripted audit -> reviewer_caught.

reviewer_caught.belongs: First caught by a genuinely separate context over the owner's artifact: adversarial reviewer, data steward, gatekeeper, or a blind second classifier - per the governance rule that a worker never reviews its own output.
reviewer_caught.does_not_belong: The owner's own pre-review checks; a steward catching its own validator's bugs (self_caught, see above).
reviewer_caught.tie_break: Both catch independently (e.g. reviewer + steward find the same defect): cite both, detection_layer = reviewer_caught (earliest independent context is a reviewer role).

owner_caught.belongs: First surfaced by the human owner (complaint, observation, or owner-side action revealing the failure).
owner_caught.does_not_belong: Owner ACTIONS taken to FIX an already-caught failure (that is fix/escalation, not detection).
owner_caught.tie_break: If the source text does not say who noticed, use the weakest defensible claim and note the uncertainty.

escaped.belongs: The failure reached output/production and caused damage with NO layer catching it at the time (discovered only retrospectively by accident, or never by the lab).
escaped.does_not_belong: Late but internal detection (that is self_caught/reviewer_caught with the delay noted in cost/notes).
escaped.tie_break: If any in-lab layer eventually caught it, it did not escape - record the catching layer and put the delay in the cost note.

late_detection.status: NOT ADDED in iteration 1 - schema-noted as an OPTIONAL v1.1 candidate per reviewer work order. Would flag records where detection lagged the onset materially (e.g. P5-F-040: 8 days); currently such lag lives in cost.value/cost.note. Decision deferred to a later audit iteration; do not emit the field yet.

field_notes.one_record_per: documented failure event or tightly-coupled defect cluster (e.g. one steward pass with N metadata rejections is one record; the cluster is disclosed in the description and notes)
field_notes.ordering: records sorted by record_id ascending; ids zero-padded P5-F-NNN and never reused
